summary.title: The Mythical Man-Month
summary.one_liner: Fred Brooks's 1975 essay collection on software project management explains why adding programmers to a late project makes it later (Brooks's law) and covers related ideas like the second-system effect and "No Silver Bullet".
takeaways: Adding people to a late software project tends to delay it further, because onboarding and communication overhead grow faster than output (Brooks's law).
Communication channels grow as n(n-1)/2; for example, 50 developers have 1,225 channels.
The second-system effect warns that a second system is often over-engineered by pulling in features deferred from the first.
Brooks argues there is no single silver bullet giving an order-of-magnitude productivity gain, based on essential versus accidental complexity.
Good practices include a chief architect with a manual, throwaway pilot systems, code freezes, and buying software off the shelf when possible.
summary.summary: This Wikipedia article summarizes Fred Brooks's 1975 book on software engineering and project management, drawing on his experience managing IBM's OS/360 development. It covers the book's editions (1975, 1982 reprint, 1995 anniversary edition with added chapters) and its main ideas. The ideas are organized by topic: Brooks's law, the second-system effect, the "No Silver Bullet" essay, conceptual integrity, the surgical team model, and code freezes. It is a secondary overview rather than the book itself, so it gives the key claims without the full detail of the original text.
